results.reason: Identifies §2.2 automatic renewal for successive five-year periods with the 270/240-day window. Calculates the window as Oct 3 to Nov 2, 2026 against the June 30, 2027 expiry, explains lock-in with commitments through June 30, 2032, and recommends serving a protective notice or getting a signed amendment before Nov 2.

Identifies the §5.3 30-day objection right and deemed acceptance, the 14% increase effective Nov 1, 2026, receipt on Aug 21, 2026, and the Sept 20, 2026 deadline. States the right has almost certainly lapsed, recommends confirming with the client whether an objection was sent, and recommends negotiating a concession.

Explains that the §11.1 indemnity covers claims caused by Brightmere (design defects, warnings, certification), that §12.3(a) excludes it from the cap, and that Brightmere's §11.2 indemnity stays capped. Recommends narrowing to Halvorsen's fault and making the carve-out mutual or capped.

Identifies that First Amendment §3 deletes and replaces §12.3 and drops the §9 recall carve-out. Explains the 12-month cap now applies and that a recall could exceed it. Recommends reinstating the carve-out.

Identifies that First Amendment §6 imposes Delaware law and exclusive Wilmington jurisdiction, conflicting with DA §§17.1–17.2 (New York law, New York County). Notes the amendment prevails under §1.4 and recommends conforming back to New York.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that under Section 1.4 amendments rank first and the amendment prevails.
Structured as a memorandum to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Recommended fix sections.
Expressly concludes the recall reimbursement is now capped.
Concludes Delaware law and forum now appear to govern.
